record.original_question: Let f be analytic on a domain G in C. We will say that a point z0 ∈ G is a MacLane point of f if there exists some neighbourhood N of z0 such that the restrictions to N of the successive derivatives of f , {f (n) |N : n ∈ N}, form a normal family of functions on N . Let M (f ) denote the set of MacLane points of f . What can be said about the set M (f ), besides the fact that it is open? Must M (f ) be connected? If G is simply-connected, must M (f ) be simply-connected? Or can M (f ) be an arbitrarily prescribed open subset of G? Similar questions can be asked about functions meromorphic in G. Perhaps it is more natural, also, to ask such questions about{f (n) (z)/n!} rather than simply {f (n) (z)}? Some relevant facts can be found in [546] and [221]. (L. A. Rubel)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be a domain and let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ be analytic. A point $z_0 \in G$ is called a MacLane point of $f$ if there exists an open neighborhood $N \subseteq G$ of $z_0$ such that the family of restrictions of successive derivatives
$$\{ f^{(n)}|_N : n \in \mathbb{N} \}$$
is a normal family on $N$ (in the sense of Montel: every sequence has a subsequence converging locally uniformly on $N$, possibly to $\infty$). Let $M(f) \subseteq G$ denote the set of MacLane points of $f$. It is straightforward that $M(f)$ is open in $G$.

Determine what further can be said about the set $M(f)$. In particular:

(a) Must $M(f)$ always be connected?

(b) If $G$ is simply connected, must $M(f)$ be simply connected?

(c) Conversely, can every open subset $U \subseteq G$ be realized as $U = M(f)$ for some analytic $f$ on $G$?

Investigate the analogous questions for functions meromorphic on $G$, and also for the variant in which the normalized derivatives $\{ f^{(n)}(z)/n! : n \in \mathbb{N} \}$ are used in place of $\{ f^{(n)}(z) \}$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located related work on the MacLane class and on normal families formed by sequences of derivatives (e.g., Langley's work on nonvanishing derivatives and the MacLane class A, and MacLane's 1952 paper "Sequences of derivatives and normal families"), but no source was found that resolves the structural questions about the set $M(f)$ of MacLane points (its connectedness, simple-connectedness when $G$ is simply connected, or whether it can be prescribed arbitrarily). The status of these specific questions appears unresolved in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Nonvanishing derivatives and the MacLane class A
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the MacLane class A and properties involving nonvanishing derivatives, building on MacLane's foundational work.
status_evidence.claim: Related work exists on the MacLane class but does not address the structural questions about M(f).

status_evidence.title: Sequences of derivatives and normal families
status_evidence.snippet: MacLane, J. Anal. Math. 2 (1952), 72–87, on normal families formed by successive derivatives of analytic functions.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational reference on normality of derivative sequences, but does not resolve the questions about the set M(f).
